subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem Addendum — operator certification & evidence handling
message_1_subject: MSA + On-Prem Addendum: operator certification & evidence handling
message_1_body:
Thanks Rachel — quick note from procurement as we finish internal review. We support Redwood overall but need clearer commitments on two items before procurement can sign:

1) Operator certification / proof of access: our InfoSec team requires a short, auditable matrix that shows what operator activities Redwood staff can perform in a private deployment and how you will provide evidence (snapshots, witness reports, logged console sessions). Is there an accepted format (spreadsheet / exhibit) you can provide?

2) License boundary for on-prem model residency: we want a single paragraph in the addendum that says allowed use cases and whether model binaries or snapshots may be retained by the customer after contract termination. Your proposed redlines left this ambiguous.

Can you attach the latest redlines and an operations-level checklist for the evidence flow? We prefer concrete answers rather than general legal language — e.g. "witnessed snapshot transfer + signed certificate" or "HSM key custody with KMS proof."

We'd appreciate a short call if useful — Chris (copied) will coordinate. Best,

— Sam Ortiz
Sr. Procurement Manager
StellarHealth
message_2_subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem Addendum: operator certification & evidence handling
message_2_body:
Thanks Sam — attaching our current redlines and an ops-level proof matrix. Quick summary up front so your team can triage: 

- Operator activities: we propose three tiers (Read-only witness, Limited operator actions, Emergency on-call ops). The matrix maps each activity to the evidence type: logged session transcripts, signed snapshot transfer manifest, notarized witness certificate.

- Snapshot custody at termination: our default is that model binaries and encrypted snapshots remain the customer's property; Redwood will not retain copies beyond a 30-day grace window used solely for orderly handover unless otherwise agreed. We can add explicit language in the addendum to capture this.

- For witnessing, we propose a "witnessing checklist" that an appointed Redwood engineer completes with customer sign-off; the checklist becomes an exhibit to the order form. That should satisfy auditors who want a chain-of-custody record.

Circling in Marissa (legal) and Alex (ops) for any legal/operational constraints. If Stellar's InfoSec prefers a different exhibit format, we can adapt — happy to jump on a 30-min call with Chris.

Thanks,
Rachel
Director, Cloud Sales
Redwood Inference
message_3_subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem Addendum: operator certification & evidence handling
message_3_body:
Sam/Rachel — I reviewed the redlines and matrix. A few legal points for the addendum we should close this week: 

1) "License boundary" language: we'll replace the ambiguous paragraph with two short clauses — (a) Permitted Use: Customer may use, copy, and execute the model artifacts for internal business purposes; (b) Post-Termination Retention: Customer may retain artifacts it received; Redwood will certify deletion of any Redwood-origin copies within 30 days except for metadata required for billing/forensics.

2) Evidence exhibits: I like the witnessed-checklist approach. Legal will need the exhibit to state that the checklist is "non-exhaustive operational evidence" and that acceptance of the checklist does not alter statutory audit rights. That phrasing keeps auditors happy without promising continuous access.

3) Escrow-like request: Stellar asked about escrow-style deposits. We cannot materially change our standard IP escrow terms without legal signoff from outside counsel. As a compromise, propose a short-run escrow-lite flow: Redwood can provide a sealed, encrypted snapshot to an agreed neutral third party under mutual-agreement triggers (bankruptcy, insolvency, breach). The customer signs an order-form exhibit with the triggers and custodian identity.

Please confirm whether Stellar will accept the escrow-lite trigger set; if yes, I'll draft the exhibit and the short clause for the addendum. 

— Marissa
VP Legal, Redwood Inference
message_4_subject: Re: MSA + On-Prem Addendum: operator certification & evidence handling
message_4_body:
Hi Sam / Chris — quick operational clarifications to help Stellar's InfoSec map requirements to evidence: 

- Witnessed snapshot transfer: our ops checklist includes SHA256 hashes, transfer manifest signed by both parties, and a short verification script we provide to confirm integrity. That covers chain-of-custody requirements without exposing Redwood internals.

- Logged sessions: we can provide redacted session transcripts and an auditor digest (hash-based) for on-demand review. Full session recordings are retained for 90 days unless longer retention is negotiated.

- Emergency access: for disaster recovery we propose a two-person Redwood/Customer witness process with time-limited credentials and full audit trails. All operator actions during an emergency are recorded and attested to in the checklist.

Next steps I suggest: (1) confirm Stellar accepts the escrow-lite triggers in Marissa's proposal; (2) legal finalize addendum language (Marissa); (3) ops sign-off on witness checklist (me) and then we circulate a single combined exhibit for signature. If acceptable, Rachel — can you propose 30-min slots tomorrow for a triage call?

Thanks,
Alex
Principal Infrastructure Engineer
Redwood Inference
